tools.name: list_workflow_templates
tools.description: The built-in starter workflows — id, name, what each does and which tools it chains. Pass an `id` to get that template’s graph back, ready to hand to `run_workflow`. This server is stateless, so these are the shipped templates only, not anything a person has saved in their own editor.

tools.name: validate_workflow
tools.description: Would this workflow graph run? Returns the blocking errors — an unknown tool, a wire into a port that does not exist, a cycle — each naming the node and the port, without running anything.

tools.name: run_workflow
tools.description: Run a workflow graph: nodes naming tools, wires carrying one node’s output into another’s input, `$whenExpression` to make a step conditional, and `scatter` to run a step once per element of a list. Returns the run record — per-node status, outputs and errors, in topological order.

tools.name: read_answer_window
tools.description: Read one window of an answer that came back cut to the size budget: the tool, the same arguments, the field its notice named, and which items or characters to return. The answer is derived again, so the window is the one that was cut.

tools.name: describe_tools
tools.description: The full description of each named tool: what it computes, its models and options, and what it refuses. The listing on this endpoint carries only each description’s opening.

tools.name: get_open_record
tools.description: Return the plasmid/sequence currently open in the editor. Emits it as a `record`, so it is the SOURCE node of a pipeline — wire its record into any downstream node's $subject.

tools.name: load_record
tools.description: Read a CHOSEN project document as a record — the pipeline's data-reader source, for running on a specific file instead of whatever happens to be open in the editor.

tools.name: list_library
tools.description: List the project's sequence documents (id, name, length, topology, kind).

tools.name: find_restriction_sites
tools.description: Cut positions of the given enzymes on the open plasmid (top/bottom cut, overhang, kind).

tools.name: find_star_sites
tools.description: Where the given enzymes could ALSO cut the open plasmid under non-standard conditions, from REBASE's own star-activity list and its one-base rule.

tools.name: check_methylation_block
tools.description: Whether the host's own methylation blocks the given enzymes ON THIS PLASMID, from REBASE's methylation-sensitivity tables localised onto your sites.

tools.name: digest_reaction_conditions
tools.description: The reaction a digest needs, from NEB's own data: the NEBuffer that serves every enzyme together (scored on the WORST enzyme's percent activity, a star-activity buffer disqualified at any percent), the incubation temperature(s), any cofactor that must be added (SAM or ATP), and each product's heat-i

tools.name: enzyme_cut_counts
tools.description: Per-enzyme cut counts on the open plasmid (the EcoRI² superscript-badge numbers).

tools.name: export_map_svg
tools.description: Render the open record's map to a publication SVG string, circular or linear — the same figure the Export panel draws, with the same knobs and the same defaults.

tools.name: run_gel_lane
tools.description: Resolve a gel lane (ladder / plasmid / digest / pcr) into [bp, form] bands for the open plasmid.

tools.name: draw_gel
tools.description: Run an agarose gel and photograph it: every lane's fragments migrated by the validated pydna model, drawn as a gel-doc image with the marker ladder's bp marks and each lane's name.

tools.name: primer_check
tools.description: Where a primer anneals on the open plasmid: 3'-anchored sites with identity % and the ✓/⚠/~/✗ verdict, graded at a bar you can move and that the answer states.

tools.name: design_oligo_plate_order
tools.description: Lay a set of oligos out as a supplier's PLATE order sheet: one worksheet per plate, in the well order the supplier's own order form fills, with the column shape its loading direction requires.

tools.name: build_genbank_submission
tools.description: Turn a record into the SUBMISSION SET NCBI's `table2asn` consumes: a `.fsa` whose defline carries the source modifiers, and a 5-column feature table (`.tbl`) beside it.

tools.name: build_ena_submission
tools.description: Turn a record into what ENA's Webin-CLI takes for an annotated sequence (`-context sequence`): an ENA flat file (`.embl`) and its manifest.

tools.name: screen_oligo_structure
tools.description: Fold a set of oligos and check them against each other: every oligo's hairpin, its self-dimer anywhere and its self-dimer at the 3' end, plus the cross-dimer with every other oligo in the set, at any position and at a 3' end.

tools.name: check_manufacturability
tools.description: Measure a sequence against what a NAMED synthesis vendor publishes it can make: length, average and windowed GC, homopolymer runs, tandem repeats, long repeats and hairpin-forming inverted repeats.

tools.name: design_gene_fragment_order
tools.description: Write the sheet IDT's gene-fragment PLATE upload takes for one or more designed fragments: one worksheet per 96-well plate, wells in the template's own order, and the template's four columns (well, name, sequence, 5' phosphorylation).

tools.name: classify_grammar_part
tools.description: Which Golden Braid / MoClo / Yeast ToolKit grammar, position and level the open plasmid represents (or null).

tools.name: align_read
tools.description: Pairwise-align ONE sequencing read against a reference and hand on the two gapped rows, so the read can be graded.

tools.name: trim_reads
tools.description: Trim sequencing adapters and low-quality ends off FASTQ reads before mapping, and report what was removed.

tools.name: fastq_qc
tools.description: FastQC's report on FASTQ reads, every module a default FastQC run reports: per-base quality boxes, per-tile quality (when the headers carry a tile), per-sequence quality, per-base sequence content, per-sequence GC against FastQC's theoretical normal, per-base N content, sequence length distribution,

tools.name: map_reads
tools.description: Map sequencing reads (FASTQ or FASTA) or assembled contigs onto a reference and return the alignment as SAM, the file a pileup viewer, a variant caller or `samtools` reads next.

tools.name: verify_read
tools.description: Grade a sequencing read against a reference (✓ verified / ⚠ near / ~ partial / ✗ divergent) from an alignment.

tools.name: read_sequencing_qc
tools.description: Read the QC files a sequencing provider returns alongside the reads: a per-base COVERAGE table, or a Plasmidsaurus summary (k-mer composition and the contamination estimate with its named source).

tools.name: domesticate_part
tools.description: Silently recode the internal Type-IIS sites inside a part's coding sequence so the part can be used in a Golden Gate assembly — same protein, no recognition site.

tools.name: design_fusion_site_primers
tools.description: Design the PCR primers that ADD Type-IIS fusion sites to a part: enzyme site, spacer and the four-base overhang you chose, on a Tm-matched annealing footprint.

tools.name: notebook_cross_refs
tools.description: Extract @plasmid / !action / &gel cross-references from a lab-notebook markdown body.

tools.name: history_protocol
tools.description: Render a construct's build history into a numbered bench-recipe protocol.

tools.name: scrub_restriction_sites
tools.description: Propose the minimal SILENT synonymous edits that remove forbidden restriction sites from a CDS (a design/write).

tools.name: fold_rna
tools.description: Minimum-free-energy secondary structure (dot-bracket + ΔG) of an RNA/DNA sequence (Turner-2004).

tools.name: pcr_amplify
tools.description: Amplify the subject template with a forward + reverse primer (pydna Anneal). Emits the first product as a NEW sequence record so downstream tools (digest, gel, map) operate on the amplicon, not the template — the tool→tool hand-off.

tools.name: design_mutagenesis_primers
tools.description: Design site-directed mutagenesis (SOE-PCR/QuikChange) primers for a point change on a CDS: the ranked inner mutagenic pairs, the constant outer pair, and the single spanning primer that replaces an outer when the site sits too near a CDS end.

tools.name: design_saturation_primers
tools.description: Design site-saturation mutagenesis (SSM) primers: one overlapping forward/reverse pair per site, each carrying a degenerate codon, sharing ONE reaction-level overlap and 3' temperature so every site amplifies in the same tube (both of Mutation Maker's solvers: fast approximation by default, exhausti

tools.name: design_multisite_primers
tools.description: Design QCLM (quick-change lightning multi-site) oligos: one primer per mutated site, all annealing in one reaction, with the codons drawn from an organism's usage table.

tools.name: reverse_complement
tools.description: Reverse-complement the subject sequence. Emits a NEW record, so downstream nodes (map, digest, gel, ORF) run on the revcomp rather than the original.

tools.name: translate_sequence
tools.description: Translate the subject DNA to protein (Biopython `Bio.Seq.translate` semantics). The SUBJECT is the selection when there is one, the named feature when `feature` is given, and the whole record otherwise — the `region` output says which, so never paste bases in to scope it.

tools.name: find_orfs
tools.description: Find open reading frames on BOTH strands of the subject (origin-spanning when circular).

tools.name: digest_fragments
tools.description: Digest the subject with the given enzymes into real fragments (sequence + both overhangs).

tools.name: gc_content
tools.description: GC fraction of the subject — whole-sequence, or a sliding window profile (DnaChisel).

tools.name: record_composition
tools.description: What the subject record is MADE OF: molecular weight under its own topology and strand count, GC and AT over the resolved bases, and the per-symbol census with the ambiguity codes broken out.

tools.name: protein_properties
tools.description: Molecular weight (average + monoisotopic), molecular formula, isoelectric point, instability index and amphipathicity (Boman index, Eisenberg hydrophobic moment) of a protein sequence (Biopython ProtParam + `peptides` + `pyteomics`).

tools.name: protein_profile
tools.description: Windowed physicochemical profile along a protein (ExPASy ProtScale). Pass `scaleId` for any of the 57 scales ProtScale publishes plus the 14 Biopython tables it does not, with optional 0-1 normalisation; or pass `kind` for the five ProtParam profiles (hydropathy over the 28 GRAVY scales, Vihinen fle

tools.name: protein_signal_peptide
tools.description: Signal-peptidase cleavage sites in a protein, by von Heijne's (1986) weight matrix as implemented by EMBOSS sigcleave.

tools.name: protein_membrane_profile
tools.description: Eisenberg hydrophobic-moment plot along a protein: per-window mean hydrophobicity and moment, each classified Globular / Transmembrane / Surface-seeking, plus those windows collapsed into residue spans.

tools.name: protein_topology
tools.description: Transmembrane topology of a protein by the HMM-TM 114-state hidden Markov model (JUCHMME, Bagos et al.), decoded residue by residue into inside / transmembrane-helix / outside runs.

tools.name: protein_disorder
tools.description: Intrinsic disorder along a protein by FoldIndex (Prilusky 2005): I_F = 2.785·⟨H⟩ − |⟨R⟩| − 1.151 over a sliding window, where ⟨H⟩ is mean normalized Kyte-Doolittle hydropathy and ⟨R⟩ the mean net charge per residue.

tools.name: protein_disorder_metapredict
tools.description: Per-residue intrinsic disorder by metapredict (Emenecker, Griffith & Holehouse, Biophys J 2021; V2/V3 the lab's successors), a bidirectional LSTM trained to reproduce a consensus of disorder predictors, run locally.

tools.name: protein_digest
tools.description: In-silico proteolytic digest of a protein (ExPASy PeptideCutter / PeptideMass): peptides with coordinates, average and monoisotopic masses, m/z per charge state, and the MS mass-window filter. 49 proteases and chemicals — or an enzyme of your own written in RPG rule grammar — one or several at a tim

tools.name: peptide_mass
tools.description: Monoisotopic and average mass of a peptide, and its m/z at each charge state (validated against pyteomics).

tools.name: fragment_ions
tools.description: Theoretical MS/MS fragment ion ladder of a peptide: a, b, c from the N-terminus and x, y, z from the C-terminus, with neutral-loss and radical variants, at each charge up to a maximum (validated against pyteomics, cross-checked against OpenMS).

tools.name: isotopic_composition
tools.description: The most probable isotopic composition of a peptide (e.g. how many 13C atoms it most likely carries) and that composition's relative abundance, from natural isotope abundances (validated against pyteomics).

tools.name: isotope_envelope
tools.description: Coarse isotope pattern of a peptide or of an elemental formula (C29H31N7O, as a compound's formula reads): the relative heights and masses of its M, M+1, M+2 … peaks as an instrument that does not resolve isotopic fine structure sees them, computed by per-element convolution from natural abundances

tools.name: score_spectrum
tools.description: Score how well an MS/MS spectrum matches a peptide with the X!Tandem HyperScore (validated against OpenMS): b and y ions are generated for the peptide, matched to the observed peaks within a tolerance, and scored as ln(1 + dot product) + ln(matched b!) + ln(matched y!).

tools.name: read_mgf
tools.description: Read the MS/MS spectra of a Mascot Generic Format (MGF) file: each spectrum's title, precursor m/z, precursor intensity, declared charge states and peak list, interpreted as pyteomics reads MGF (validated on every spectrum of PXD000001).

tools.name: read_mzml
tools.description: Read the spectra of a PSI mzML run file: each spectrum's native id, MS level, centroid or profile, scan start time and unit, base peak, total ion current, precursor (selected ion m/z, charge, intensity, isolation window) and peak arrays, interpreted as pyteomics reads mzML (validated on every spectr

tools.name: infer_proteins
tools.description: Protein inference from peptide-spectrum matches (validated against OpenMS BasicProteinInferenceAlgorithm on PXD000001): maps each peptide to the protein database, keeps the best match per spectrum, scores each protein by aggregating its peptides' best scores, reports the proteins its evidence cannot

tools.name: bayesian_protein_inference
tools.description: Bayesian protein inference, Epifany (validated against OpenMS BayesianProteinInferenceAlgorithm on PXD000001): the posterior probability that each protein, each indistinguishable group and each peptide-spectrum match is present, from the matches' posterior error probabilities under a network in whic

tools.name: target_decoy_qvalues
tools.description: False discovery rate and q-values for peptide-spectrum matches by target-decoy competition (validated against pyteomics): give each match's score and whether it hit a decoy; returns every match's q-value, the whole set's FDR, and how many targets pass a q-value threshold.

tools.name: crispr_design_guides
tools.description: Design and score CRISPR guides on the subject — on/off-target scores, QC flags, and cloning-enzyme conflicts.

tools.name: crispr_design_library
tools.description: Turn the open record's annotated targets into an ORDERABLE sgRNA oligo pool: the best N guides per target, filtered at order time (Pol-III terminator, Graf inactive motif, cloning-enzyme site, minimum on-target score), each composed into the oligo a synthesiser makes — the vector's cloning overhangs

tools.name: crispr_analyze_screen
tools.description: Call HITS from a pooled CRISPR screen: per-guide read counts in, a gene-level Bayes factor and a precision/recall curve out.

tools.name: design_knockout_package
tools.description: The complete build package for a knockout or knock-in, as one object: guides inside the target, an off-target census for the chosen one within this molecule, a repair template with real homology arms, a screening PCR whose primers sit OUTSIDE the arms, the protocol in order, the fragments and oligos

tools.name: screen_guides
tools.description: Screen guide spacers the way CHOPCHOP does before it accepts them: GC gate, self-complementary hairpins inside the spacer, and hairpins against the sgRNA backbone.

tools.name: search_off_targets
tools.description: Search a sequence for sites a guide could also cut, allowing mismatches, and score each one (MIT and CFD) plus the aggregate specificity of the guide WITHIN that sequence.

tools.name: survey_off_targets
tools.description: Count every guide's off-target sites by mismatch class across one sequence, in one pass — the question that comes BEFORE opening any single guide's site table: which of these spacers is worth looking at.

tools.name: fold_guide
tools.description: Fold a guide RNA — the spacer alone, and the whole sgRNA on a real published scaffold — and report which bases of the spacer pair with the scaffold.

tools.name: list_sgrna_scaffolds
tools.description: Every sgRNA scaffold this workbench has sourced, with the nucleases each covers and the publication it comes from.

tools.name: scan_splice_sites
tools.description: Find the splice sites a sequence accidentally spells - the check a codon-optimised CDS needs before it goes into a plant or any other eukaryotic host, because a synonymous swap chosen for codon usage or GC can spell a donor or acceptor that was not there before, and the transcript is then spliced so

tools.name: scan_motif_sites
tools.description: Find every place a transcription-factor binding motif (a position-frequency matrix, such as a JASPAR matrix's counts) matches a DNA sequence, on both strands, at a threshold set per motif as a fraction of that matrix's own score range.

tools.name: scan_sigma70_promoters
tools.description: Find σ70 (housekeeping) promoters in a bacterial sequence and say how strong each one is, using the published La Fleur-Hossain-Salis biophysical model - six interaction motifs (UP element, -35, spacer, extended -10, -10, discriminator) plus the R-loop strength of the first transcribed bases, fitted

tools.name: scan_intrinsic_terminators
tools.description: Find rho-independent (intrinsic) transcription terminators in a bacterial sequence: a stem-loop followed by a thymine-rich tail, scored by TransTermHP's published model (Kingsford, Ayanbule & Salzberg 2007).

tools.name: score_rbs
tools.description: Score the ribosome-binding site already in front of a start codon: the Shine-Dalgarno hybridisation energy, the mRNA folding that competes with it, the spacing it implies, and the resulting relative initiation strength.

tools.name: assemble_operon
tools.description: Stack several CDSs into one contiguous operon, designing a fresh ribosome-binding site in front of each one AGAINST ITS REAL UPSTREAM CONTEXT — which is why the RBS for gene 2 is not the RBS design_rbs would give it in isolation.

tools.name: codon_usage_analysis
tools.description: Codon-usage analysis of an in-frame CDS: CAI / expression stats, GC, and every rare-codon occurrence for the chosen organism (pydna port), plus the two bias measures that need NO reference table — ENC (Wright 1990) and RCBS (Roymondal 2009), which are therefore computable for any organism.

tools.name: codon_usage_distance
tools.description: How this region's codon usage compares with the record's OTHER genes (CUFS, Diament, Pinter & Tuller 2014).

tools.name: check_invariants
tools.description: Decide whether a sequence is scientifically admissible: protein unchanged, forbidden restriction sites absent, reading frame intact, length/GC/CAI inside stated bounds.

tools.name: design_expression_variants
tools.description: The expression-design deliverable: several coding sequences for one protein, each variant following a different published strategy (maximise codon adaptation, match the host's codon usage, harmonise with the native host, or preserve the initiation region), each scored by an engine — CAI, GC, the fol

tools.name: optimize_sequence
tools.description: Run the DnaChisel optimizer over the subject with real constraints/objectives (GC window, pattern avoidance, translation enforcement, …).

tools.name: design_rbs
tools.description: Design a 5'UTR (Shine-Dalgarno + spacer) in front of a CDS to hit a target translation-initiation strength (SC-08 engine, Turner-2004 folding).

tools.name: design_lamp_primers
tools.description: Design LAMP (loop-mediated isothermal amplification) primer SETS - four core oligos (F3 · B3 · FIP · BIP) plus optional loop primers, judged against Eiken's own PrimerExplorer V5 criteria.

tools.name: design_codehop
tools.description: Design CODEHOP hybrid oligos from a block of aligned PROTEIN - for homologues too diverged for nucleotide-level design to see at all.

tools.name: design_degenerate_primers
tools.description: Design degenerate primers from a multiple-sequence ALIGNMENT - the 'amplify every homologue in this family' question, which a single-template designer cannot answer because it only ever sees one sequence.

tools.name: design_bisulfite_primers
tools.description: Design BSP or MSP primers for a methylation assay, on the CONVERTED strands: after bisulfite treatment every unmethylated C reads as T, which is a different template from the one every other designer sees.

tools.name: design_sequencing_primers
tools.description: Design a WALK of sequencing primers that reads a whole region, not one pair: tiled reads with confirmed overlap, on both strands by default, plus the coverage the walk actually achieves and any stretch it cannot reach.

tools.name: design_primers
tools.description: Design a forward + reverse primer pair to amplify the subject (pydna `primer_design`), with Tm, Ta and suggested Taq/Phusion cycling programs.

tools.name: align_sequences
tools.description: Multiple-sequence alignment over several sequences, under either of TWO engines that answer different questions and neither of which is a fallback for the other.

tools.name: draw_alignment
tools.description: Draw a block of an alignment as an SVG figure: the rows named, the residues shaded by how much of their column agrees with them, the column numbers over the block and Easel's Clustal conservation line under it.

tools.name: alignment_redundancy
tools.description: Find the rows of an alignment that repeat another: each row's redundancy is its highest percent identity to a row at least as long (ungapped residues), and a row at or above the threshold is redundant, so filtering keeps the longest representative of each near-identical group.

tools.name: alignment_pca
tools.description: Principal component analysis of the rows of an alignment: the pairwise similarity of every two rows under PID or a substitution matrix (BLOSUM62, PAM250 for protein; Jalview's DNA matrix for nucleotides), decomposed into eigenvectors, and each row's coordinate on the leading components, so rows that

tools.name: read_structure_consensus
tools.description: Read the consensus RNA secondary structure a Stockholm alignment states in its `#=GC SS_cons` line (WUSS, the notation Rfam and Infernal write), and measure how well the aligned rows actually support it.

tools.name: gibson_assemble
tools.description: Assemble fragments by terminal homology (Gibson / NEBuilder / In-Fusion, DnaCauldron).

tools.name: assemble_multiple_inserts
tools.description: Open ONE circular backbone at several places and place several inserts in a single step.

tools.name: design_gibson_primers
tools.description: Design the PCR primers that CREATE the terminal homology a Gibson/NEBuilder/In-Fusion assembly needs: a Tm-matched pair per fragment, each carrying the 5' overhang that fuses it to its neighbour in the order given (pydna assembly_fragments).

tools.name: golden_gate_assemble
tools.description: Assemble parts with a Type-IIS enzyme (Golden Gate / MoClo, DnaCauldron). Emits the first construct as a NEW record for downstream nodes.

tools.name: check_golden_gate_parts
tools.description: Check parts BEFORE a Type-IIS assembly: how many recognition sites each carries, which of them are the two deliberate flanking sites and which are internal sites that will mis-cut the part.

tools.name: score_overhang_fidelity
tools.description: Score a Golden Gate junction (fusion-site) set against MEASURED T4 DNA ligase end-joining data.

tools.name: design_split_sites
tools.description: Decide where to CUT one sequence into Golden Gate fragments, optimising the split positions and the overhangs they create together.

tools.name: design_overhang_set
tools.description: Design a high-fidelity Golden Gate overhang set of a given size against measured ligation data, optionally pinning junctions you cannot change (a fixed vector's own overhangs).

tools.name: assembly_plan_simulate
tools.description: Run a MULTI-LEVEL assembly plan (DnaCauldron `AssemblyPlan`): several assemblies arranged into dependency levels, where each level's products become parts for the next.

tools.name: melt_profile
tools.description: DNA melting behaviour of the subject by the Poland–Scheraga model (DECIPHER): the melt curve (mean helicity vs temperature), its Tm50, and the cooperatively-melting domains behind each HRM peak.

tools.name: design_ish_probes
tools.description: Design an in-situ hybridization probe against the subject: tile it into candidate oligos that meet a melting-temperature, G+C and composition specification, screen them for off-target binding against an alignment and for k-mers abundant in a reference, and gather the survivors into the set that imag

tools.name: design_padlock_probes
tools.description: Design padlock probes for in-situ sequencing against the subject: find the two-arm targets whose melting temperature falls in a window, check each against a BLAST search for any other transcript that could be ligated across the junction, pack non-overlapping targets from the 3' end, and assemble eac

tools.name: design_hcr_probes
tools.description: Design HCR v3.0 split-initiator probe pairs against the subject: tile its reverse complement into 52 nt windows, drop windows with C or G runs, a stable hairpin, G+C or RNA:DNA free energy outside their windows, or (given a bowtie2 alignment of the tiles) more than one genome hit, then pick non-over

tools.name: design_merfish_probes
tools.description: Design MERFISH encoding probes for the subject transcript: tile it into target regions, keep those whose G+C and melting temperature fall in their windows, that share no k-mer with an rRNA or tRNA, and whose k-mers occur in this gene's transcripts and nowhere else in the transcriptome; attach readou

tools.name: design_xenium_probes
tools.description: Design Xenium custom-panel padlock targets on the subject transcript to 10x Genomics' published rules (CG000683): two 20 nt arms whose primer3 melting temperatures fall in their windows, a ligation-junction dinucleotide the Xenium ligase accepts, no run of five G in the probe, at least four mismatch

tools.name: design_genetic_circuit
tools.description: Design a genetic circuit that computes: give it a logic function and it synthesizes a NOR/NOT netlist, assigns real characterized repressor gates from a Cello UCF library, predicts the dynamic range between ON and OFF, and emits the construct's DNA.

tools.name: dot_plot
tools.description: Self-similarity or pairwise comparison of the subject as a dot plot — repeats, inversions and shared regions.

tools.name: dot_plot_grid
tools.description: All-against-all dot plot over a sequence SET — EMBOSS `polydot`. Every ordered pair is plotted with the exact k-mer engine and laid out as an N×N grid, so shared regions, repeats and inversions across a whole family are visible in one picture.

tools.name: build_tree
tools.description: Build a phylogeny from aligned sequences — distance methods (NJ, BIONJ, FastME, UPGMA/WPGMA), parsimony, maximum likelihood, or Bayesian MCMC under a strict clock and coalescent prior — with branch support from a bootstrap, aLRT or aBayes, or, for the Bayesian method, clade posterior probabilities.

tools.name: select_substitution_model
tools.description: Choose the substitution model for a maximum-likelihood phylogeny by fitting every candidate — model x rate-heterogeneity x invariant-sites — on ONE shared topology and ranking them by AIC, AICc or BIC with Akaike weights.

tools.name: transform_tree
tools.description: Edit a tree that is already built — re-root it (at its midpoint, on an outgroup, or remove the root), prune taxa away or down to a set, ladderize it, or collapse branches that are too weakly supported or too short to believe.

tools.name: draw_tree
tools.description: Draw a tree as an SVG figure — rectangular, slanted, circular or unrooted, as a phylogram or a cladogram, with tip names, branch support and a scale bar.

tools.name: compare_trees
tools.description: Compare trees over the same taxa: the Robinson-Foulds distance between two of them, and the consensus of any number.

tools.name: tree_statistics
tools.description: Describe a tree without rebuilding it: its shape statistics (tips, height, balance, the gamma statistic), the lineages-through-time curve, and the patristic distance matrix — the path lengths through the tree, which is what to compare against the alignment distances that built it.

tools.name: tree_taxon_annotations
tools.description: Read what a NeXML tree file says about each of its taxa: every annotation on every OTU (an NCBI taxon, a rank, a parent taxon), one row per annotation, plus how many distinct values each property takes.

tools.name: export_tree
tools.description: Convert a tree between the four formats this workbench reads and writes — Newick, NEXUS, PhyloXML and NeXML — sniffing the input format rather than making the caller declare it.

tools.name: audit_barcodes
tools.description: Check an index set you ALREADY have, rather than designing a new one: the minimum distance between any two, how many errors that guarantees correcting, the full distance matrices, and — optionally — the subset that survives pruning to a stricter error budget.

tools.name: demultiplex_reads
tools.description: Assign reads to the index each one came from, and say how many could NOT be assigned reliably — a hit further from a barcode than the set's guaranteed correction radius is not that barcode, and counting it as one is how a demultiplexing report hides a failed run.

tools.name: export_barcodes
tools.description: Write an index set out in the form the next step needs: a CSV or TSV order sheet, FASTA, an IDT bulk-input sheet of the bare tags, an Illumina BCLConvert SampleSheet, or the actual oligos — adapters built on a template, or primers carrying the tag — with the junction warnings that emission produces.

tools.name: design_barcodes
tools.description: Design a set of NGS sample-index barcodes with a guaranteed minimum distance, and report what that set actually corrects — substitutions, or indels too (DNABarcodes).

tools.name: design_qpcr_assay
tools.description: Design qPCR assays over the subject — primer pair plus hydrolysis probe, ranked by penalty, with amplicon size/GC, per-oligo Tm and whether both primers bind a single site.

tools.name: check_scorpion_stem
tools.description: A Scorpion probe's two melting temperatures, side by side: the stem-loop's own hairpin and the duplex the loop makes with its target on the amplicon.

tools.name: simulate_taqman_curve
tools.description: Predict the amplification curve a hydrolysis-probe (TaqMan) qPCR assay will draw, and the Cq read off it, from the assay's own sequences and its thermocycling programme - a forward simulation, not a fit to data.

tools.name: call_cq
tools.description: Amplification curves to Cq, one row per reaction. tools.name: analyze_melt_curves
tools.description: Melt curves to melting temperature, under any of THREE engines that answer different questions and none of which is a fallback for another.

tools.name: propagate_uncertainty
tools.description: Uncertainty through any qPCR quantity, three independent ways at once. tools.name: rank_tradeoffs
tools.description: Which candidates in a table are not beaten on every objective at once: Pareto (non-dominated) sorting of rows scored on several columns, each to maximize or minimize.

tools.description: Solve C₁V₁ = C₂V₂ for whichever of the four quantities is left empty (stock concentration, stock volume, final concentration, final volume), each in its own unit: molar (M to fM), mass per volume (mg/mL to ng/mL), fold (X) or percent.

tools.description: Plan a serial dilution: the same fold dilution repeated tube after tube from a stock, each tube made to one volume.

tools.name: convert_mass_moles
tools.description: Convert a mass of a molecule to an amount in moles and a number of molecules, or an amount back to a mass.

tools.name: plan_thermocycler_program
tools.description: Plan the cycling programme for an amplicon on a NAMED enzyme, and check the reaction against that manufacturer's own published limits.

tools.name: recombine

tools.name: rank_strategies
tools.description: Compare EVERY assembly chemistry this engine has against one set of parts, and say what each one costs and risks.

tools.name: ligate_fragments
tools.description: Ligate fragments by their overhangs (pydna ligation_assembly) — sticky, optionally blunt.

tools.description: Cut and ligate in ONE POT (pydna restriction_ligation_assembly): every input is digested by the same enzymes inside the reaction and the pieces are joined as they appear, so a junction that re-forms a recognition site can be cut again.

tools.name: ligation_independent_clone
tools.description: Join fragments without a ligase by one of the five named methods — LIC, SLIC, In-Fusion, CPEC or USER (pydna).

tools.name: design_ligation_independent_primers
tools.description: Design the PCR primers a ligation-independent reaction needs — LIC, SLIC, In-Fusion, CPEC or USER: a Tm-matched pair per amplified fragment, in the order given.

tools.name: fusion_pcr
tools.description: Overlap-extension (fusion) PCR — join fragments that share terminal homology into one product, carrying their features across (pydna).

tools.name: design_combinatorial_library
tools.description: Design a combinatorial library in one step: SLOTS, each offering a bin of interchangeable parts, plus the CONSTANTS every member carries.

tools.name: check_value
tools.description: A QC gate. Compares a wired value against a threshold and PASSES or FAILS the pipeline there — every node downstream of a failed gate is skipped, so a run stops at the first check that does not hold.

tools.name: filter_items
tools.description: Keep only the rows of a table-shaped output that meet a condition — the bands above a size, the guides over a score, the assays under a penalty.

tools.name: get_selection
tools.description: The region selected on the canvas, as its own record. This is what makes a highlighted stretch a pipeline INPUT: wire its record into any node's subject and that step runs on the selection rather than on the whole molecule.

tools.name: pick_first
tools.description: Rejoin two branches: takes the outputs of several conditional steps and emits the first one that actually ran.

tools.name: check_rows
tools.description: A QC gate over a TABLE: assert something about every row at once (every band inside a size window, no guide above an off-target score, at least three assays under a penalty).

tools.name: summarize_rows
tools.description: Reduce a whole TABLE column to one number — the largest band, the median guide score, the spread of a set of melting temperatures.

tools.name: multiplex_pcr
tools.description: Screen a primer POOL against one or more templates: every predicted product, per-primer off-target binding, the pairs that tell templates apart on a gel, and the all-against-all primer-dimer matrix a pool actually lives or dies by (pydna primer_screen + primer3 thal).

tools.name: antibody_liabilities

tools.name: humanize_antibody

tools.name: graft_antibody_cdrs
tools.description: Humanize an antibody variable domain by CDR grafting: find the closest human germline V and J, merge them into an acceptor framework, and put the parental CDRs onto it.

tools.name: antibody_isotype
tools.description: Name the CONSTANT region of an antibody chain: which immunoglobulin gene and allele it carries (IGHG1, IGHA2, IGKC, IGLC2 …), and where each IMGT domain sits on it — CH1, the hinge, CH2, CH3, the secretory tail and the membrane exons, or the single C region of a light chain.

tools.name: antibody_molecule

tools.name: antibody_antigen_contacts

tools.name: compare_antibodies

tools.name: antibody_canonical_classes

tools.name: antibody_position_frequencies
tools.description: How common each residue of an antibody variable domain is at its IMGT position, and which residues are rarer there than a cut (abYsis's 1% "unusual residue" by default).

tools.description: Differential expression from raw RNA-seq read counts, by one of the three standard count models.

tools.name: discover_gene_tree_discordance
tools.description: Find the genes whose own alignment rejects the species tree. Each named alignment file is one gene, its records the taxa, named as the species tree's tips.

tools.description: Ask whether the genes used to normalize expression (reference or housekeeping genes, such as GAPDH, ACTB or B2M) are more or less variable across human tissues than genes of the same abundance, on GTEx v8 median expression.

tools.description: Find the signal peptides or transmembrane segments in reviewed human UniProt that a sequence predictor contradicts.

tools.name: rank_next_tests
tools.description: Rank candidate experiments by what running them would TEACH — Lindley's expected information gain, the drop in uncertainty about a hypothesis expected before anything is run.

tools.description: The design step's view of a discovery corpus: each record's name, file, length and GC fraction, and how many records each file holds.

tools.description: Fetch a real codon-usage table for an organism and save it into this project, so later steps can score against it by name.

tools.description: Resolve an organism to its published genome assemblies and the chromosomes, plasmids and organelles each one is made of, with every accession and length NCBI reports.

tools.name: search_records
tools.description: Search the sequence archives by free text (a gene name, a protein, an organism, a phrase) across NCBI Nucleotide and Protein, ENA (plain records, WGS and TSA/TLS assembly sets, and annotated coding/non-coding features), UniProtKB and the iGEM Registry at once, and hand back the matching accessions.

tools.name: fetch_record
tools.description: Fetch a sequence by accession from an authoritative archive (NCBI Nucleotide or Protein, ENA, UniProtKB, the iGEM Registry, Addgene, or the EBI Dbfetch gateway) and hand it downstream as a real record with its annotations.

tools.name: list_samples
tools.description: Browse the bundled sample library: the real bio files a new project can start from (GenBank and SnapGene plasmids, FASTA sets, alignments, Sanger traces, structures, variant calls and more), each with its id, format and size, and its archive provenance where the corpus records one.

tools.description: Identify a stretch of DNA by asking the iGEM Registry which published part carries exactly those bases, and hand back that part's own description, Sequence-Ontology role, literature citation and license.

tools.description: Ask one of the ~60 authoritative databases a question and hand its rows downstream — Ensembl, UniProt, ClinVar, gnomAD, ChEMBL, PubChem, InterPro, STRING, PDB, AlphaFold, the GWAS Catalog, PubMed and the rest.

tools.description: Fetch a paper's whole open-access text from Europe PMC by PMCID or PMID: title, authors, journal, license, abstract, every section and every figure caption, as Markdown.

tools.description: Find the sequence accessions a text names (a paper's methods, a notebook, a report) and resolve each against its archive: identifiers.org's own pattern for every namespace a fetch target serves, scanned over the text, then one batched search per archive.

tools.description: Read one region of ClinVar's monthly release VCF, as the VCF ClinVar publishes: its header, then every record overlapping the region, through the release's tabix index so only those blocks are fetched.

tools.description: Compare a SET of sequencing reads against one reference in ONE shared frame: align every read to the reference, vote a consensus column by column, and report the positions where the reads differ from it, each with the change it makes to the protein.
